title: Mini-batch credit catalog — back-of-envelope
content:
Purpose
Quick personal scratchpad for a credit/catalog approach that biases customers toward mini-batching and credit packs. Goal: simple UX for self-serve, predictable unit economics for hosted offering, and an easy upgrade path to Dedicated for heavy sustained throughput.

High-level idea
- Sell pre-bundled "mini-batch" credit packs (token-equivalent) priced to nudge batching and compact prompts.
- Include a small bucket of free/minimal credits in Starter to hook developers.
- Overages billed at a predictable per-1k-token rate or consumed from next pack.
- Provide explicit recommendations in the Console: suggested batch size, quantization tier, and model family for the pack.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope)
- Typical request: 40 prompt tokens + 160 response tokens = 200 tokens per call.
- Average tokens per minute per active developer: 10k tokens (very variable).
- Infra cost estimates per 1k tokens (approx current internal numbers, round):
  - 7B family (optimized): $0.0008 per 1k tokens
  - 13B family: $0.0022 per 1k tokens
  - 70B family: $0.0090 per 1k tokens
- Target gross margin (hosted API): 3x markup on infra cost (so price ≈ infra * 3) to cover SW/HW ops, SRE, and growth CAC.

Suggested retail per-1k-token pricing (rounded)
- 7B: $0.0025 per 1k tokens
- 13B: $0.007 per 1k tokens
- 70B: $0.027 per 1k tokens

But the product is credits/packs, not raw per-token pricing. Packs should create mental anchors and FOMO on discounts for buying bigger packs.

Pack ideas (tokens expressed in thousands):
- Pocket: 50k tokens — price = 50 * 0.0025 * 0.9 = $0.1125 (i.e. $0.11) for 7B-equivalent credit (use 10% pack discount to encourage buy).
- Dev: 250k tokens — price = 250 * 0.0025 * 0.85 = $0.53 (15% discount).
- Team: 1M tokens — price = 1000 * 0.0025 * 0.80 = $2.00 (20% discount).
- Scale: 10M tokens — price = 10000 * 0.0025 * 0.70 = $17.50 (30% discount).

Observation: absolute prices are tiny because infra cost per token is very small. UX implication: represent packs in 'credits' where 1 credit = 1k tokens, and show USD price with friendly rounding. Otherwise micro-prices feel weird.

Credit mapping proposal
- 1 credit = 1k tokens at 7B-default conversion.
- Model multipliers: 13B consumes 2.6 credits per 1k tokens (reflects infra ratio), 70B consumes 11 credits per 1k tokens.
- When user purchases a Pack (e.g., Team = 1000 credits), Console shows equivalent runtime throughput per model family and recommended batch settings.

Example experience (Developer buying Dev pack)
- Dev buys 250 credits for $0.60 (rounding upward from $0.53).
- Console recommends: use 13B with mini-batch size 4, or 7B with batching=1 for lower cost.
- If they select 13B, consumption multiplier applies; a 200-token call counts as 0.2 credits * multiplier.

Edge economics and margin checks
- If 1 credit = $0.0009 infra (approx), but we sell at $0.0009*3 = $0.0027, pack discounts reduce margin; ensure Scale pack margin is >= 2x infra cost on average.
- Example worst-case: All pack consumed on 70B (multiplier 11). Then effective infra spend for 1k user-tokens = 11 * infra_7B ≈ 11 * 0.0008 = $0.0088 vs price per credit discounted to $0.00175 (with 30% discount) — loss. So need guardrails.

Guardrails to avoid loss-making pack consumption
- Define pack flavor: packs are tied to model families or include a model-family cap. E.g., Team (7B) vs Team-Pro (13B) vs Team-XL (70B).
- Or require explicit upgrade step to buy multi-model pack; default pack rates apply only to 7B.
- Or allow pack consumption across families but apply conversion multiplier and bill the difference at checkout if pack insufficient (this is complex UX).

Alternate simpler approach (recommended for MVP)
- Packs are 7B-equivalent credits. If user uses 13B/70B, they pay an overage multiplier on live billing (not pack). Packs only cover 7B consumption. This prevents hidden losses and keeps pricing simple.

Tier skeleton (MVP)
- Starter (free): 25 credits / month, console guidance, rate limit 60 r/min, no SLA.
- Developer (paid): 250 credits one-time or subscription monthly, overage = per-1k-token price (explicit), support via docs.
- Team: 1k credits monthly (subscription) + discounted overage. Optional seat add-ons.
- Enterprise: custom, includes Dedicated options, committed capacity discounts, Audit & KMS add-ons.

Additional levers and experiments to run
- Offer burst-credit trial: small temporary 5k credits that expire in 7 days to encourage exploration of higher-cap models.
- Offer bonus credits for integration events (e.g., first convo with Redwood chat SDK gives +50 credits).
- Price anchoring: show per-1k-token equivalent savings vs pay-as-you-go.
- UX nudge: suggest "switch to 7B with larger batch" when pack consumption > 70% to steer users to cheaper mode.

Metrics to track (quick list)
- Pack conversion rate (visit -> buy) and churn on monthly packs.
- Avg tokens consumed per customer per 30d window, broken down by model family.
- Margin per pack (actual infra spend vs revenue) monthly.
- % of pack consumed on higher-cost models (13B/70B).

Open questions / TODOs
- How to present fractional USD values clearly? Round up to cents or show credits as the primary unit?
- UX for mixed-model usage: allow packs to be consumed across families or not? If allowed, how to protect margin? (ask finance/ops)
- What conversion multipliers are accurate on current runtime with batching? Need SRE/applied-ML to run controlled benchmark and produce per-1k-token cost across typical batching distributions. (ticket: JIRA-PRIC-142)
- Decide expiration policy for credits: 12 months vs 90 days vs non-expiring for subscription. Pros/cons: breakage vs liability.

Notes to self
- Prototype in Console: pack purchase flow + a usage breakdown widget showing "pack remaining if you use X model at Y batch size".
- Experiment: small A/B where Dev pack either covers 13B at 1.5x multiplier vs only 7B. Measure upgrades to Team pack.
- Coordinate with growth on simple email copy for encouraging batching tips.

Rough next steps
1) Ask Applied-ML to run per-1k-token cost matrix under small/medium/large batch profiles for 7B/13B/70B. 2) Wire an internal calc in the Console prototype that uses multipliers and shows customer-facing estimates. 3) Draft pricing text and internal guardrail policy and review with finance.

End scratchpad — lots of small assumptions here; primary constraint is preventing packs becoming a loss vector for high-cost models. Keep initial launch packs conservative (7B-equivalent) and iterate.
